CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Patient presents with acute sub-sternal tightness radiating to left shoulder and intermittent shortness of breath for 36 hours. Secondary complaint of chronic mechanical lower back stiffness.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Ms. Vance reports acute onset of pressure-like retrosternal chest pain (7/10 severity) starting yesterday evening, exacerbated by deep inspiration. Associated with mild dyspnea and diaphoresis. Denies recent trauma. Has history of chronic lumbar strain for which she takes occasional ibuprofen.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
- Vitals: BP 142/88, HR 94 regular, RR 20, SpO2 96% on room air, Temp 98.6F.
- Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, normal S1/S2, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
- Respiratory: Decreased breath sounds at right lung base, mild inspiratory wheeze, no crackles.
- Musculoskeletal: Paraspinal lumbar tenderness without radiculopathy.

DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP ORDERED:
1. 12-lead ECG (CPT 93000) - normal sinus rhythm.
2. Chest Radiograph Single View (CPT 71045) - ordered STAT to rule out acute pneumothorax, pulmonary consolidation, or thoracic aortic pathology given acute chest discomfort.

ASSESSMENT & PLAN:
1. Acute Chest Pain, unspecified (ICD-10: R07.9) - Primary etiology for urgent imaging. Stat chest radiograph ordered to evaluate pulmonary parenchymal infiltration or acute cardiothoracic etiology.
2. Dyspnea, unspecified (ICD-10: R06.02) - Secondary respiratory symptom.
3. Low back pain (ICD-10: M54.5) - Incidental chronic baseline complaint, stable, conservative management continued.
